title: Functions and Straight-line Graphs (y = mx + c)
kicker: Cambridge Lower Secondary · Mathematics 0862 · Stage 8 · Algebra
summary: Use function machines and inverse operations, write real situations as y = mx + c, plot straight-line graphs from tables of values, and read the gradient and y-intercept.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Understand that a function is a rule where each input gives exactly one output. Work out outputs from inputs, and work backwards with inverse operations to find the input from an output — including with fractions. [8As.03]
Turn a situation described in words into a linear function y = mx + c, and describe a function y = mx + c as a real situation in words. [8As.04]
Use coordinate pairs to make a table of values for a function such as y = 3x − 2, and plot its straight-line graph. [8As.05]

Know that every equation y = mx + c gives a straight line, where m is the gradient (how steep the line is) and c is the y-intercept (where it crosses the y-axis), for whole-number values of m. [8As.06]

blocks.text: A **function** is a mathematical machine: you put a number in, it does the same operations every time, and one number comes out. When you write a function as y = mx + c and plot the input–output pairs as coordinates, you always get a straight line. This page takes you from function machines to tables of values, straight-line graphs, and the meaning of m and c.
1. Key words

items: function
دالة — a rule that gives exactly one output for each input
input / output
المدخل / المخرج — the number you put in / the number you get out
function machine
آلة الدالة — a diagram showing the operations in order
inverse
العكسي — the operation that undoes another; used to work backwards
mapping, x → 2x + 1
تحويل — another way to write a function: "x maps to 2x + 1"
table of values
جدول قيم — a table of x values and the y values they give
coordinates (x, y)
إحداثيات — a point: across first, then up or down
linear
خطي — makes a straight-line graph
gradient, m
الميل — how steep a line is: change in y ÷ change in x
y-intercept, c
الجزء المقطوع من محور y — where the line crosses the y-axis, the point (0, c)
parallel
متوازي — lines that never meet; they have the same gradient

blocks.text: 2. Functions and function machines

In a function, **each input has exactly one output**. Put 5 into the machine below and you always get 13 — never anything else. A rule like "output any number bigger than the input" is **not** a function, because one input could give many different outputs. (Two different inputs giving the same output is allowed: x → 4 sends every input to 4.)

blocks.caption: The function y = 3x − 2 as a machine (top) and its inverse (bottom).

items: **Finding an output:** follow the arrows. Input 5: 5 × 3 = 15, 15 − 2 = 13.
**Finding an input:** start at the output and go backwards, using the **inverse** of each operation in **reverse order**. Output 22: 22 + 2 = 24, 24 ÷ 3 = 8. So the input was 8.
The same function can be written as a machine, as a mapping **x → 3x − 2**, or as an equation **y = 3x − 2**.
Inputs can be negative or fractions: input −1 gives −3 − 2 = −5; input 1/2 gives 1 1/2 − 2 = −1/2.

blocks.text: **Fractions in the machine.** For the machine "× 3/4, then + 1": input 8 → 8 × 3/4 = 6 → 6 + 1 = 7. To find the input for output 4, go backwards: 4 − 1 = 3, then the inverse of × 3/4 is ÷ 3/4, which is the same as × 4/3: 3 × 4/3 = **4**.

**Finding the rule from a table.** If the inputs 1, 2, 3, 4 give outputs 5, 8, 11, 14, the outputs go up by 3 when the input goes up by 1, so the rule starts "× 3". Then 1 × 3 = 3 and we need 5, so "+ 2". The function is y = 3x + 2. (This is the same method as finding the nth term of a sequence.)
3. From words to y = mx + c (and back)
Many real situations are linear: there is a **starting amount** and then a **fixed amount for each unit**. The fixed amount per unit is m; the starting amount is c.

rows: A taxi charges $4 to start plus $2 per kilometre.
A tank holds 500 litres and drains at 20 litres per minute.
A plant is 6 cm tall and grows 3 cm each week.

blocks.text: **Going back to words.** For y = 5x + 30 you could write: "A gym charges a $30 joining fee and then $5 for each visit. y is the total cost in dollars for x visits." Explain what x and y stand for, and where the 5 and the 30 appear in your story.
4. Tables of values and plotting a straight line

items: Make a table with the x values you are given (for example from −2 to 3).
Substitute each x into the function to find y. Take care with negative numbers.
Write the coordinate pairs (x, y).
Plot each point with a small, neat cross.
Join the points with a **ruler** — one straight line through all of them, going right to the edges of the x range. Label the line with its equation.
If one point is not on the line, check that calculation again — the points of y = mx + c are always in a straight line.

blocks.text: 5. Gradient and y-intercept
Every straight line (except a vertical one) has an equation **y = mx + c**.

items: **c is the y-intercept**: the line crosses the y-axis at (0, c). Put x = 0: y = m × 0 + c = c.
**m is the gradient**: for every 1 step to the right, the line goes up m steps. Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x (rise ÷ run).
m positive → the line goes **up** from left to right. m negative → it goes **down**. m = 0 → it is horizontal (y = c).
A bigger number for m (ignoring the sign) means a **steeper** line. y = 5x is steeper than y = 2x.
Lines with the **same gradient are parallel**.

blocks.text: On y = 2x + 1 the green triangle goes 2 units right (run) and 4 units up (rise), so the gradient = 4 ÷ 2 = **2**. ✓

rows: vertical line: not of the form y = mx + c

blocks.text: **Finding the equation from a graph:** (1) read c where the line crosses the y-axis; (2) choose two points where the line crosses grid corners exactly; (3) gradient = change in y ÷ change in x (negative if the line goes down); (4) write y = mx + c.
**Is a point on the line?** Substitute the x-coordinate. Is (4, 9) on y = 2x + 1? 2 × 4 + 1 = 9 ✓ — yes. Is (4, 10)? No, because y would be 9, not 10.

blocks.title: افتكر y = mx + c
items: c = النقطة اللي الخط بيقطع فيها محور y (لما x = 0).
m = الميل: كل ما تمشي خطوة واحدة يمين، الخط بيطلع m خطوات (ولو m سالبة بينزل).
خطين ليهم نفس الـ m يبقوا متوازيين.
الدالة: كل مدخل ليه مخرج واحد بس. ولو عايز ترجع من المخرج للمدخل، اعكس العمليات وابدأ من الآخر.

blocks.text: 6. Worked examples

**Worked example 1** — A function machine multiplies by 4 and then subtracts 5. (a) Find the output when the input is −2. [1] (b) Find the input when the output is 19. [1] (c) Find the input when the output is 0. [1]
Common mistake: going backwards in the wrong order (19 ÷ 4 first, then + 5). Undo the LAST operation FIRST.
**Worked example 2** — A function is x → (2/3)x + 1. (a) Find the output when x = 9. [1] (b) Find x when the output is 5. [2]
**Worked example 3** — (a) Complete the table of values for y = 3 − 2x. [2] (b) Draw the graph for x from −1 to 3. [2]
Working: x = −1: 3 − 2 × (−1) = 3 + 2 = 5. x = 3: 3 − 6 = −3. The line goes **down** because the gradient is −2, and it crosses the y-axis at 3.

**Worked example 4** — A candle is 30 cm tall when it is lit. It burns down 2 cm every hour. (a) Write a function for its height h cm after t hours. [1] (b) What do the gradient and the y-intercept mean? [2] (c) After how many hours is the candle 12 cm tall? [1]

rows: Starts at 30, goes down 2 each hour: **h = 30 − 2t** (or h = −2t + 30)
Gradient −2: the height goes down by 2 cm each hour. y-intercept 30: the height at the start (t = 0) is 30 cm.

items: The line crosses the y-axis at (0, −2), so c = −2.
From (0, −2) to (2, 4): run = 2, rise = 4 − (−2) = 6. Gradient m = 6 ÷ 2 = 3.
Equation: **y = 3x − 2**. Check with (2, 4): 3 × 2 − 2 = 4 ✓

blocks.text: **Worked example 6** — Here are four equations: A: y = 4x − 1  B: y = x + 4  C: y = 4x + 3  D: y = −1 − 2x. (a) Which two lines are parallel? [1] (b) Which line has the same y-intercept as line A? [1] (c) Does the point (−3, −13) lie on line A? Show how you decide. [1]

rows: A and C both have gradient 4, so **A and C** are parallel.
A crosses at −1. D = −2x − 1 also crosses at −1: **D**.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Working backwards through a machine in the wrong order. Undo the last operation first.
Negative x values: 3 − 2 × (−1) = 5, not 1; 2 × (−2) + 1 = −3, not 5.
Joining points by hand, with a wavy line, or stopping the line at the last point instead of the whole x range.
Reading the gradient from y = 5 − 2x as 5. Rewrite as y = −2x + 5: m = −2, c = 5.
Forgetting the sign of the gradient: a line going down from left to right has a negative gradient.
Gradient as run ÷ rise. It is change in y ÷ change in x.
Mixing up coordinates: (3, 1) means 3 across, 1 up — not 3 up.

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: "Complete the table of values" then "Draw the graph of y = … on the grid": each correct value and a ruled line through correct points earn marks.
"Find the input when the output is …" — show the inverse operations.
"Write down the gradient / y-intercept of the line y = …" — 1 mark each; rearrange to y = mx + c first.
"Draw a ring around the equation of the line that is parallel to …" or "Match each equation to its graph": compare m (steepness, up or down) and c (crossing point).
"Does the point (…) lie on the line? Show how you decide" — substitute and state Yes or No.
Word problems: "Write a formula/function for …", then "What does the number … represent?" — answer in the context (cost per km, starting height…).

questions.q: A function machine multiplies by 5 and then adds 3. What is the output when the input is −4?
A function machine multiplies by 3/4 and then subtracts 1. The output is 8. What was the input?
Which table could NOT show a function?
questions.e: In a function each input has exactly one output. In the second table the input 4 gives two different outputs (2 and −2), so it is not a function. Different inputs giving the same output (third table) is allowed.

What is the gradient of the line y = 7 − 3x?
questions.e: Rewrite as y = −3x + 7. The number multiplying x is the gradient: m = −3. (7 is the y-intercept.)

questions.q: Write down the y-intercept of the line y = 5x − 8.
questions.e: In y = mx + c, c is the y-intercept. Here c = −8: the line crosses the y-axis at (0, −8).

questions.q: Write down the coordinates of the point where the line y = 3x + 6 crosses the x-axis.
questions.e: On the x-axis, y = 0. So 3x + 6 = 0 → 3x = −6 → x = −2. The point is (−2, 0).

questions.q: Which line is parallel to y = 3x + 2?
questions.e: Parallel lines have the same gradient. y = 3x + 2 has gradient 3; so does y = 3x − 5. (y = −3x + 2 and y = 2 − 3x have gradient −3.)

questions.p: A plumber charges a fixed fee of $25 plus $15 for each hour of work. C is the total charge in dollars and h is the number of hours.
questions.q: (a) Write a formula for C in terms of h.
questions.e: $15 for each hour gives 15h; add the fixed fee of 25: C = 15h + 25.

blocks.title: Remember
items: A function gives exactly one output for each input. To go backwards, use inverse operations in reverse order.
In real situations y = mx + c: m is the amount per unit (rate), c is the starting amount.
Table of values → coordinate pairs → neat crosses → one ruled straight line across the whole range.
y = mx + c: m = gradient (rise ÷ run; negative means downhill), c = y-intercept (0, c).
Same gradient → parallel lines. To test a point, substitute its x-coordinate.
